key_points: Normal BP: below 120/80 mmHg
Elevated BP: 120–129 / below 80 mmHg
Hypertension Stage 1: 130–139 / 80–89 mmHg
Hypertension Stage 2: 140/90 mmHg or higher
Hypertensive Crisis: above 180/120 mmHg — refer immediately
scenarios.sop_excerpt_en: Bangladesh NCD referral guidelines: CHW should refer any patient with BP >= 140/90 to Upazila Health Complex. Pregnancy with BP >= 140/90 with symptoms is a hypertensive emergency requiring immediate referral.

bangla_card.title: Blood Pressure Levels and Referral
bangla_card.body:
Normal: below 120/80
Stage 1: 130–139 / 80–89
Stage 2: 140/90 or higher
Crisis: above 180/120 — refer immediately
bangla_card.next_step: If BP is 140/90 or higher, refer to the Upazila Health Complex

key_points: Advise low-salt diet — less than 5 g salt per day
Encourage daily walking or moderate activity for 30 minutes
If prescribed medication, stress that it must be taken daily — even when feeling well
Avoid tobacco and alcohol
Weight reduction helps: every 5 kg lost lowers BP by about 5 mmHg
Refer if BP ≥ 140/90 at follow-up despite lifestyle advice
scenarios.sop_excerpt_en: Lifestyle modification is the first-line intervention for Stage 1 hypertension. Medication adherence counselling is critical — CHW should use teach-back to confirm understanding.

bangla_card.title: Counselling: High Blood Pressure
bangla_card.body:
1. Less salt in food — less than 5 g per day
2. Walk 30 minutes every day
3. Take medicine every day if prescribed — do not skip
4. Do not smoke or drink alcohol
5. Weight loss helps lower blood pressure
bangla_card.next_step: If BP is still 140/90 at next visit, refer to the Upazila Health Complex

key_points: Antihypertensive medication must be taken every day, even when blood pressure feels normal
Stopping medication without doctor advice can cause BP to spike
Common side effects: dizziness when standing — advise to stand up slowly
If patient misses a dose, take as soon as remembered — do not double dose
Keep a pill calendar to track daily intake
scenarios.sop_excerpt_en: Medication adherence is the leading cause of uncontrolled hypertension in community patients. Teach-back with pill calendar demonstration increases adherence.

bangla_card.title: Taking BP Medicine Every Day
bangla_card.body:
• Take your BP medicine every day — even when you feel well
• Do not stop medicine without asking your doctor
• If dizzy when standing, stand up slowly
• If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember
• Use a calendar to track your medicine
bangla_card.next_step: Check if patient has their medicine and how many days' supply remain

key_points: Normal fasting glucose (FBS): below 5.6 mmol/L
Pre-diabetes FBS: 5.6–6.9 mmol/L
Diabetes FBS: 7.0 mmol/L or higher
Normal random glucose (RBS): below 7.8 mmol/L
Diabetes RBS: 11.1 mmol/L or higher with symptoms
scenarios.sop_excerpt_en: Diabetes diagnosis thresholds for Community Health Workers in Bangladesh. FBS >= 7.0 mmol/L on two separate occasions or RBS >= 11.1 mmol/L with classic symptoms confirms diabetes.

bangla_card.title: Diabetes Test Thresholds
bangla_card.body:
Fasting Blood Sugar (FBS):
• Normal: below 5.6 mmol/L
• Pre-diabetes: 5.6–6.9 mmol/L
• Diabetes: 7.0 mmol/L or higher

Random Blood Sugar (RBS):
• Diabetes: 11.1 mmol/L or higher (with symptoms)
bangla_card.next_step: If FBS is 7.0 or RBS is above 11.1, refer to a doctor

key_points: Advise patient to eat smaller meals at regular intervals — avoid large gaps between meals
Reduce white rice, white bread, sweets, and sugary drinks
Increase vegetables, lentils, and high-fibre foods
Daily walking 30–45 minutes lowers blood sugar
Foot care is important — check feet daily for wounds or sores
If hypoglycaemia (dizziness, sweating, shaking) — eat sugar immediately and refer
scenarios.sop_excerpt_en: Lifestyle counselling for diabetes patients. Foot care education is a critical component — diabetic foot wounds are a common cause of hospitalisation in Bangladesh.

referral_threshold.condition: Hypoglycaemia symptoms or foot wound present

bangla_card.title: Counselling: Diabetes Care
bangla_card.body:
1. Eat smaller meals every 4–5 hours
2. Eat less white rice, sweets, and sugary drinks
3. Walk 30–45 minutes every day
4. Check your feet every day for wounds or sores
5. If dizzy and sweating, eat sugar immediately
bangla_card.next_step: If foot wound found or patient dizzy and sweating, refer immediately

key_points: Danger signs in pregnancy requiring immediate referral
Severe headache with visual disturbance → pre-eclampsia
BP >= 140/90 in pregnancy → hypertensive disorder
Vaginal bleeding at any stage → emergency
Reduced or absent fetal movement → emergency
Swelling of face and hands → possible pre-eclampsia
scenarios.sop_excerpt_en: Maternal health danger signs for Community Health Workers. Any pregnant woman with severe headache, visual disturbances, BP >= 140/90, vaginal bleeding, or reduced fetal movement must be referred immediately to the nearest facility.

referral_threshold.condition: Any of the listed danger signs present

bangla_card.title: Danger Signs in Pregnancy
bangla_card.body:
Refer immediately if any of these signs are present:
• Severe headache or blurred vision
• Blood pressure 140/90 or higher
• Vaginal bleeding
• Reduced or absent fetal movement
• Abnormal swelling of face and hands
bangla_card.next_step: If any danger sign is present, refer immediately to the nearest health facility

key_points: At least 4 ANC visits are required: at 16, 24–26, 32, and 36 weeks
Ask about bleeding, swelling, headache, or reduced fetal movement since last visit
Check blood pressure and weight at every visit
Offer iron and folic acid tablets — confirm patient is taking them
Discuss birth preparedness plan: transport, support person, facility
scenarios.sop_excerpt_en: ANC visit preparation checklist for CHW home visits. Birth preparedness discussion should happen at the 32-week visit at the latest.

bangla_card.title: Preparing for an ANC Visit
bangla_card.body:
Ask about:
• Bleeding, headache, or swelling since last visit
• Fetal movement felt?
• Is she taking iron and folic acid tablets?

Check:
• Blood pressure and weight

Discuss:
• Transport plan for delivery
• Who will accompany her?
bangla_card.next_step: If BP >= 140/90 or any danger sign, refer immediately

quiz_questions.question_bangla: A patient's blood pressure is 160/100 mmHg. Where would you refer them?
options_bangla: Refer only if symptoms are present
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: When BP is 140/90 or higher, refer to the Upazila Health Complex. 160/100 is Stage 2 — high risk.
140/90 mmHg or higher is Stage 2 hypertension and requires referral.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: Which symptom in hypertension indicates an emergency?
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: Severe headache and blurred vision are signs of a hypertensive emergency. Refer immediately.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: A patient with Stage 1 hypertension asks how much salt is safe per day. What is the correct answer?
options_bangla: No limit — salt does not affect blood pressure
Only avoid adding salt at the table
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: The guideline recommends less than 5 g of salt per day to help reduce blood pressure.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: Which lifestyle change has the most direct impact on lowering blood pressure?
options_bangla: Reducing salt and doing daily exercise
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: Reducing salt intake and daily moderate exercise (30 minutes walking) have the strongest evidence for lowering blood pressure.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: A patient says their BP feels normal so they stopped taking medication. What do you advise?
options_bangla: It is fine to stop if BP feels normal
They must keep taking medicine every day — stopping can cause BP to spike
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: BP medicine must be taken every day, even when the patient feels well. Stopping suddenly can cause a dangerous BP spike.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: A patient on BP medicine feels dizzy when they stand up. What advice do you give?
options_bangla: Stand up slowly and hold onto something
Lie down for the rest of the day
Drink more water and eat more salt
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: Postural dizziness is a common side effect of antihypertensives. Advise standing up slowly — do not stop the medicine without consulting the doctor.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: What fasting blood sugar level confirms a diabetes diagnosis?
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: FBS of 7.0 mmol/L or higher on two occasions confirms diabetes.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: What is the main warning sign of diabetes?
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: Excessive thirst, frequent urination, and fatigue are classic symptoms of diabetes.
FBS of 5.6–6.9 mmol/L indicates pre-diabetes. Advise lifestyle changes and regular monitoring.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: A diabetes patient has a wound on their foot but says it does not hurt. What do you do?
options_bangla: Advise them to monitor it at home — no pain means it is not serious
Clean it and recheck in a week
Refer immediately — diabetic foot wounds can become serious even without pain
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: Diabetes can reduce pain sensation in the feet. Even a painless wound must be referred promptly as it can become infected and serious.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: A diabetes patient is dizzy, sweating, and shaking. What is the first step?
options_bangla: Advise them to lie down and rest
Give them sugar immediately (sweet drink or candy), then refer
Ask them to fast until the dizziness passes
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: Dizziness, sweating, and shaking are signs of hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar). Give sugar immediately, then refer.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: A pregnant patient has BP 150/95 and a headache. What do you do?
options_bangla: Schedule a routine follow-up next week
Advise rest and recheck in 3 days
Refer immediately to the Upazila Health Complex
Give aspirin and monitor at home
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: BP >= 140/90 with headache in pregnancy is a sign of pre-eclampsia. Immediate referral is required.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: Which symptom during pregnancy is a danger sign requiring immediate referral?
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: Blurred vision and severe headache are danger signs of pre-eclampsia. Refer immediately.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: What should you do if vaginal bleeding occurs at any stage of pregnancy?
options_bangla: Monitor at home if the amount is small
Tell the patient to go to the clinic the next day
Refer immediately to the nearest health facility
Refer only if bleeding occurs in the first trimester
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: Vaginal bleeding at any stage of pregnancy is an emergency. Refer immediately.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: How many ANC visits are recommended during a normal pregnancy?
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: At least 4 ANC visits are recommended at 16, 24–26, 32, and 36 weeks of pregnancy.

quiz_questions.question_bangla: Which item must you discuss with the pregnant patient at the birth preparedness visit?
options_bangla: Transport plan and who will accompany her to the facility
quiz_questions.explanation_bangla: Birth preparedness includes confirming transport arrangements and who will support the patient — this must be discussed by the 32-week visit.
